_comment: An Age where bows stand opposite its light in the weather that makes one.
The word rather than the page: `rainbow` is the aspect's own aiming page, minted by
`Vocabulary.aimingPages`, and an aspect already is its page -- so `art/word/rainbow.json` is a
collision the vocabulary refuses outright. This is what asks for one without aiming at it, and the
plural is what keeps the two legible side by side: `red and yellow rainbow` describes one, and
`a rainbows Age` says the Age has them.
It *names* the phenomenon rather than searching for one (design 8.1), as `auroral` does and for the
same reason: a bow is the one thing this word means, so it arrives with its answer in hand where a tag
query would also have found whatever else was bright and colourful.
**It says one thing and touches one aspect, deliberately.** A narrowing word is priced in its
lowest-ordinal aspect (`Resolver.pricedIn`) and phenomena are last, so the obvious second thing to
want here -- a rainfall bound, a bow needing rain -- would quietly reprice this as a word about the
weather. That is why the rain lives on `Phenomenon.RAINBOW.insistsOn` instead: a floor on the Age's
own weather, and the one phenomenon for which a floor is the right shape rather than the wrong one.
